# Printing, display, and friendly errors {#sec-printing}

- The user-experience release: fix how greta arrays, models, and MCMC
  results print, and make errors and checks helpful. Grouping labels:
  the `printing` and `error-handling` clusters. Some of these are the
  package's best contributor on-ramps.
- Several depend on the same underlying decision: whether to base
  greta's array/unknowns classes on `vctrs` ([#648](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/648)), which unlocks the
  clean printing edge cases.

**Both remaining breaking changes land here.** [#648](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/648) is one of them, and
[#692](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/692) - which triangle
greta's cholesky factor uses - is the other. [#692](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/692)'s *work* belongs with
the distributions milestone (@sec-distributions) and its representation
machinery; it is written up here because the plan batches the two
breaking changes into one release, so that users migrate once rather
than twice. That makes this the milestone with the largest migration
burden in the plan, and the natural 1.0 candidate whenever greta
decides to go there. It is not going there yet.

### [Issue #257](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/257)

- 2018-11-21
- documentation
- Users want greta to play nicely with tidyverse/tidymodels idioms.
- problem: no documented bridge between greta objects and tidy tooling.
- finding: mostly a documentation + light-shim task; overlaps the docs lane.
- **the central claim is verified, and the vignette is unblocked today.** `tidybayes::tidy_draws()`, `spread_draws()`, `gather_draws()` and `ggmcmc::ggs()` all work on greta draws with **zero greta changes**. The specific gap is real too: `as.data.frame(draws)`, `as_tibble(draws)` and `broom::tidy(draws)` all fail with "cannot coerce class `greta_mcmc_list`".
- **the fix document omits `{posterior}`**, which already provides a complete tidy bridge — `posterior::as_draws_df()` works, and `summarise_draws()` returns mean/sd/q5/q95/**rhat**/**ess** in a tibble, i.e. much of what a "tidy summary" and [#439](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/439) would want. Add `posterior` to the Suggests list and cover it in the vignette as the modern standard.
- also worth doing: greta arrays in tidyverse verbs **silently produce all-`NA`** rather than erroring (`as_tibble`, `as.data.frame`, `data.frame`, `tibble`, `mutate` — all "succeed"). A plausible-looking all-NA data frame with no warning is arguably worse than a failure. An `as.data.frame.greta_array` that errors with a pointer to `calculate()` would kill the trap.
- fix: a "greta and the tidyverse" vignette (tidybayes/ggmcmc/posterior over the existing `coda::mcmc.list`) plus cheap `as.data.frame`/`as_tibble` methods for `greta_mcmc_list` (thin wrappers over `as.matrix()`, which works); keep the return type unchanged per maintainer guidance, don't add arguments to core functions.
- proposed fix: see [fixes/issue-257.md](fixes/issue-257.md).
- priority: medium.
- defect in the proposed fix: the acceptance test in `fixes/issue-257.md` does not run. It builds on `distribution(as_data(rnorm(10))) <- normal(mu, 1)`, which parses but fails at runtime with *"target of assignment expands to non-language object"* - a replacement function needs an assignable name on the left, so the test fails at model definition, before reaching the behaviour under test. Assign first: `y <- as_data(rnorm(10))`, then `distribution(y) <- normal(mu, 1)`.

### [Issue #615](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/615)

- 2024-02-12
- Up Next, low hanging fruit
- Misspelt argument names pass silently.
- problem: no early check for unknown argument names.
- finding: unknown named args (e.g. `nsims`) fall into `...` and are treated as targets, tripping `check_greta_arrays()` (`R/calculate.R:192`) with a misleading message. Fits the checking layer alongside [#784](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/784).
- **the premise is stale: it does not pass silently, it errors.** `calculate(x, nsims = 5)` aborts, **names the offending argument**, and points at the right call frame (unlike [#784](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/784)). The residual gap is narrow — there is no "did you mean `nsim`?" suggestion, and the hint that is given ("Perhaps you forgot to explicitly name other arguments?") points the user in the *opposite* direction from the actual mistake. Retitle from "pass silently" to "no did-you-mean suggestion for near-miss argument names".
- **the proposed `agrep(max.distance = 0.34)` is unsafe — verified.** `max.distance` is a *fraction of pattern length*, so short names match nearly everything: `sd`, `x` and `n` each match all six `calculate()` formals, `mu` matches three, and `beta` matches `trace_batch_size`. Those are exactly the names users give greta arrays, so `calculate(x, sd = 3)` would suggest "did you mean `trace_batch_size`?" — worse than the status quo. The `are_greta_array()` pre-filter contains the blast radius (these are already errors) but degrades the message.
- fix: add a `check_dots_misspelled()` helper that matches non-greta-array `...` names against the real formals using a **bounded `utils::adist()`** — threshold <= 2, plus a guard requiring the candidate be within ~2 characters of the formal's length — and aborts with a "did you mean `nsim`?" hint; wire it into `calculate()`. Pin the false-positive cases above as tests. Confirmed formals: `values`, `nsim`, `seed`, `precision`, `trace_batch_size`, `compute_options`.
- proposed fix: [fixes/issue-615.md](fixes/issue-615.md)
- priority: medium (good contributor task).
- defect in the proposed fix: `agrep(max.distance = 0.34)` is unsafe. `max.distance` is a *fraction of pattern length*, so short names match nearly every formal: `sd`, `x` and `n` each match all six of `calculate()`'s formals, and `beta` matches `trace_batch_size`. Those are precisely the names users give greta arrays, so `calculate(x, sd = 3)` would suggest "did you mean `trace_batch_size`?" - worse than the status quo. Use a bounded `utils::adist()` (threshold <= 2, plus a length guard), and pin those false positives as tests.

### [Issue #692](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/692)

- 2024-08-13
- (none)
- greta's cholesky factor should be upper triangular, as `base::chol()` returns.
- problem: R's `chol()` returns an upper triangular factor. greta should match it, so that a factor obtained from a greta model can be used with `backsolve()`/`forwardsolve()` on the same assumptions as a factor from base R.
- finding: **the July 2026 pass recorded this as fixed, and that verdict was wrong.** It tested `chol()` on a *data* greta array - `all.equal(calculate(chol(as_data(K)))[[1]], chol(K))` is `TRUE` - but the issue is about the *variable* path, which is the case its own reprex shows: `wishart(df = 4, Sigma = diag(3))`, where greta holds a cholesky factor internally as its representation of the variable. The data path was already correct and was never what the issue asked about. The maintainer's ruling (August 2026) is that [#692](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/692) is not resolved.
- fix: establish which triangle the variable path returns for `wishart()`, `lkj_correlation()` and `cholesky_variable()`, and make it upper to match the data path and base R. Land a regression test pinning `chol()` against `base::chol()` at the same time - the risk runs in both directions, because greta.gp does `Lm <- t(chol(Kmm))` and then `forwardsolve(Lm, ...)`, which needs a lower factor and works only because the data path is upper. Flipping a convention without the test would make greta.gp **silently return wrong numbers**: measured at a maximum absolute difference of 0.2961 on a 4x4, with no error raised.
- priority: high. This is one of the two known breaking changes left in the plan, and it is batched with [#648](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/648) so both land in one release.

### [Issue #784](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/784)

- 2025-03-26
- (none)
- `calculate()` produces the wrong error message.
- problem: `check_dependencies_satisfied()` (`R/checkers.R:699-780`) builds a good `final_msg` (which mentions `nsim`) but then `rlang::abort()`s with the worse `msg`, uses a broken pluralisation count (`length(names_text)` on a joined string), and defaults `call` to the `lapply` frame.
- finding: a message-only fix, no behaviour change (confirmed by reading the discarded `final_msg`).
- fix: abort with `final_msg`, count `length(unmet_names)`, and pass an explicit `call` from `calculate()` so the backtrace points at `calculate()` not `lapply`.
- proposed fix: [fixes/issue-784.md](fixes/issue-784.md)
- priority: medium (quick).
